text.p: Troubled Paul Gascoigne survived as a member of England's soccer squad on Friday and was told by coach Glenn Hoddle that he could become a role model.

Gascoigne, who was last month accused in newspapers of beating up his wife and sent off for kicking an opponent while playing for Rangers against Ajax Amsterdam in the European Champions' League, was retained for a World Cup European group two qualifier in Georgia on November 9.
"It would have been the simple thing for me to have cast him out," Hoddle said. "To punish him now would have been easy, not just for me but for Paul as well.
"We have chosen the more difficult way...the tougher way for Paul. Long term, he can become a role model off the back of the mistakes he's made."

Hoddle, a committed Christian, instigated counselling for 29-year-old Gascoigne, always a controversial figure during his career with Newcastle, Tottenham Hotspur, Lazio of Rome and now Scottish champions Glasgow Rangers.

Gascoigne has not denied allegations of beating his wife Sheryl, who was pictured in newspapers two weeks ago with a marked face, an arm in a sling and heavily bandaged. Gascoigne has also admitted heavy drinking.

"I have sat in on some of the counselling," Hoddle said. "Sometimes the meetings lasted as long as five hours. I have begun to understand Paul's problems. He knows he has got to change. He has started to react positively."
Hoddle agreed drink was "a slight problem" but insisted it was not the major issue.
"Much of what I have learnt has to remain private," he said.

"My first concern two weeks ago was for Paul and his family. I have been deeply impressed by his determination to address his problems. I believe that with my help and counselling we can guide and help both him and his family to go further. I will certainly do everything I can for them.
"I do not condone what Paul has done. I also accept that people are human."

Women's groups reacted angrily to Gascoigne's reprieve. Julie Bindel, a spokeswoman for an international conference on violence and abuse of women, said: "Hoddle has clearly shown that football and winning a match are more important than the safety of women."

Two Arsenal players who have admitted alcoholism were named by Hoddle: Paul Merson and former captain Tony Adams, who is recalled after recovering fitness and, with Alan Shearer out injured, could be a candidate to lead his country again for the match in Tbilisi.
Shearer's place in the squad as a striker is taken by another Arsenal player, 32-year-old Ian Wright, who won the last of his 20 caps two years ago.
